q: nag-overheat ang makina, pwede bang buhusan ng tubig?
source: How to check your engine coolant - The AA
steps: If the temperature gauge rises, turn the heater up full as a temporary fix.
A red temperature light means pull over somewhere safe.
Switch off and let the engine cool for at least 30 minutes, longer if it overheated.
Don't remove the radiator or coolant cap unless the engine is cold: pressurised hot water can scald.
When cold, check the coolant tank is between min and max; water only as an emergency top-up.
Have the car checked at a garage: coolant should not drop.
title: Engine overheating

q: may nahimatay, hindi humihinga si lola
source: How to do CPR | St John Ambulance
steps: Make sure it's safe; shake their shoulders and ask loudly "are you OK?"
No response: shout for help, tilt the head back, check normal breathing for up to 10 seconds.
Not breathing normally: have someone call 911 on speaker and find a defibrillator.
Heel of your hand mid-chest, other hand on top, arms straight, press down 5–6 cm.
Push 100–120 times a minute. Not trained? Keep giving continuous chest compressions.
Continue until help takes over, they breathe normally, or you are exhausted.
title: CPR (adult, not breathing)

q: May metal sheet na nakasugat sa akin
steps: Wash and dry your hands; wear disposable gloves if you have them.
Press on the wound with a bandage or clean folded cloth.
If something is stuck in it, leave it in and press firmly on either side.
Raise an injured arm above head level; for a leg, lie down and raise it above the heart.
If blood soaks through, add another pad on top and keep pressing.
Every 10 minutes check the bandage isn't too tight.
title: Cuts and bleeding

steps: Face: has one side of the face drooped? Ask them to smile.
Arms: can they lift both arms and keep them up? One may be weak or numb.
Speech: is their speech slurred or confused?
Time: call 911 straight away, even if the signs stop. Note the time they started.
Don't drive them to the hospital yourself if an ambulance can come; follow the call handler's instructions.
title: Stroke: think FAST
